title: AI Is Taking Over Physics and Nobody Talks About It
research:
This is a Sabine Hossenfelder video (mid/late Aug 2026 in this scenario) whose math section matches almost verbatim her newsletter post 'Conscious Feedback, Roasted Dinosaurs, & The End of Mathematics' (Aug 19, 2026, https://sciencewtg.substack.com/p/conscious-feedback-roasted-dinosaurs), which links every named source: graduate student Tasmin Chu on 'existential crisis'/'moratorium on using LLMs to prove novel mathematical theorems' (https://tasmin.substack.com/p/more-calls-to-action-for-the-mathematical; also https://siliconreckoner.substack.com/p/news-rumors-gossip confirming she is a Caltech grad student); assistant professor Max Weinreich's preprint making 'the case for total opposition to the use of artificial intelligence in mathematics' (arXiv 2608.02859); postdoc Alexis Marchand arguing LLMs are evil on climate grounds (https://proofsandprompts.com/2026/08/14/mathematicians-machines-and-the-earth/); PhD student Kirwin Hampshire (Univ. of Victoria) 'The Dark Night of Mathematics', 'going insane', 'profound spiritual crisis' (https://kirwinhampshire.substack.com/p/the-dark-night-of-mathematics); and Daniel Litt's talk 'The End of Mathematics' (https://www.daniellitt.com/blog/2026/8/11/the-end-of-mathematics) with exactly the 'no one will read, no one will care, no one will benefit' framing. The transcript renders these names phonetically (Tasman Chu, Maximilian Reich, Alexis Machete, Kerwin Hampshire), i.e. ASR artifacts of the correct people.

Jacobian conjecture: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced (July 19, 2026) an explicit three-variable counterexample credited to Claude Fable 5; the conjecture (Keller's problem) dates to 1939, i.e. 87 years (https://theconversation.com/hello-there-the-jacobian-conjecture-is-false-thanx-why-a-tiny-social-media-post-has-mathematicians-rethinking-ai-283883, https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/07/21/claude-s-fable-5-just-solved-an-87-year-old-math-problem-and-it-matters-for-bitcoin, https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/07/21/a-digestion-of-the-jacobian-conjecture-counterexample/).

OpenAI Astra: On Aug 1, 2026 OpenAI published 'Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science' claiming an internal, unreleased Astra model produced results on ten problems open a decade or more, with Lean 4 certificates; no peer review yet (https://the-decoder.com/openai-announces-its-next-major-model-astra-by-dropping-ten-previously-unsolved-math-solutions/, https://tech-insider.org/openai-astra-solves-10-open-math-problems-2026/).

30-year-old conjecture: Dmitry Rybin used GPT-5.6 Pro (four prompts) to construct a counterexample to the ~30-year-old Dinitz–Garg–Goemans conjecture, July 22, 2026 (https://officechai.com/ai/mathematician-says-gpt-5-6-disproved-the-30-year-old-dinitz-garg-goemans-conjecture-with-4-simple-prompts/).

Riemann: Anthropic announced Aug 10–11, 2026 that an unreleased research Claude raised the unconditional lower bound for zeta zeros on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%, with Lean formalization and external reviewers Conrey and Goldston (https://www.anthropic.com/research/riemann-zeta, https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/no-ai-didnt-just-solve-the-thorniest-problem-in-math/).

Physics: Peter Woit's post 'HEP-TH and AI' (https://www.math.columbia.edu/~woit/wordpress/?p=15818) shows hep-th submissions (excluding cross-lists) for the past three months about 1/3 higher than previous years; a summary of this very Hossenfelder video says the spike was ~30% above prior-year baselines in May and June (https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/ai-research/2026/physicists-use-llms-skip-the-panic). Maxwell: 'The Maxwell Conjecture is False' (arXiv:2607.27197, July 29, 2026) by three authors, Philip Arathoon, Gavin Ball, Matthew D. Kvalheim, exhibits five charges with ≥24 non-degenerate critical points, refuting Maxwell's 1873 (n−1)² bound; the authors state the idea for the construction was suggested by an LLM, reported as GPT-5.6 Sol (https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27197v1, https://officechai.com/ai/gpt-5-6-sol-helps-mathematicians-prove-that-150-year-old-maxwell-conjecture-is-false/, https://www.datacamp.com/blog/gpt-5-6-sol-and-maxwell-conjecture). Membranes: arXiv:2607.29348 'Mode-dependent photothermal responsivity mapping of tensile-stressed nanomechanical resonators' explicitly states 'This model was derived with the help of Claude Fable 5 from Anthropic' (https://arxiv.org/html/2607.29348). The Adesso claim (Nottingham, ChatGPT 5.6 central contribution to the proof strategy of an entanglement no-go result, all steps checked by him) is reported in coverage of this video (startuphub.ai) but I could not locate the primary preprint; Adesso is indeed a Nottingham quantum-information researcher working on entanglement. The other short physics examples (LLMs for symbolic/high-precision HEP computations, Claude for numerical quantum calculations, Claude writing ion-transport software for a trapped-ion computer, a GPT agent selecting stellarator designs) are echoed in that coverage but I found no independent primary sources; they are consistent with the documented 2026 pattern (e.g. https://www.science.org/content/article/chatgpt-spits-out-surprising-insight-particle-physics, https://openai.com/index/new-result-theoretical-physics/).

comparisons.claim: Claude Fable 5 helped find a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture.
The Jacobian conjecture had been an open problem since 1939.
OpenAI announced 10 results from its still unreleased model called Astra, each of which either solved or advanced long-standing open mathematical problems.
A group used ChatGPT to disprove a 30-year-old conjecture.
Graduate student Tasman Chu called for a moratorium on using LLMs to prove novel mathematical theorems.
Assistant Professor Maximilian Reich wrote a preprint arguing for total opposition to the use of artificial intelligence in mathematics.
Postdoc Alexis Machete argued that LLMs are evil because they contribute to the climate crisis.
PhD student Kerwin Hampshire stated he is suffering a profound spiritual crisis due to AI developments in mathematics.

Assistant Professor Daniel Litt gave a talk about the end of mathematics, arguing that AI will lead to the production of mathematically correct results that no one will read, care about, or benefit from.
The arXiv category hep-th stands for high energy physics theory.
Gerardo Adesso is a physicist at the University of Nottingham.
Gerardo Adesso proved that there is no easier way to create certain complicated entangled quantum states, and he did so with the help of ChatGPT 5.6.
Gerardo Adesso stated that the AI made a central contribution to developing the proof strategy for his result on entangled quantum states.
James Clerk Maxwell proposed a rule for how many equilibrium points (where electric forces cancel) can arise from a given number of electric charges.

Three researchers showed that Maxwell's rule for the number of equilibrium points from a collection of electric charges is wrong, and their paper states the key idea behind the construction was suggested by ChatGPT 5.6.

Two researchers studying how tiny silicon membranes behave when illuminated by a laser developed a model derived with the help of Claude Fable 5, and the model has excellent agreement with observations.
A paper in high energy physics used several large language models to carry out symbolic and high precision numerical computations.
A paper in quantum physics used Claude for numerical calculations.
A team had Claude write software for moving ions around inside a quantum computer.
In fusion research, a ChatGPT agent was used to decide which stellarator designs to try next.
Anthropic announced that Claude had made a major advance on the Riemann zeta function, working towards the Riemann hypothesis.

Peter Woit examined the number of submissions to the arXiv preprint server in the category hep-th (high energy physics theory) and found that submissions were up about 30% in May and June compared to previous years.
